source_span: The curve continues to price a reopening of the Strait of Hormuz and lower oil prices ahead. That expectation has repeatedly been pushed back.
source_chain: Futures curve prices a Strait-of-Hormuz reopening and falling Brent (spot $96 vs six-month ~$83), and that relief keeps failing to arrive, therefore if the blockage persists the back end must reprice higher, removing a support for equities/credit right as cross-asset vol has already collapsed into 'complacency.' Invalidation: the blockage actually lifting / Mideast supply recovering, letting the curve's relief pricing prove correct.
pulse_chain: Brent cleared $100 this morning against Goldman's $85 December forecast (raised this week), and JPM/GS energy inputs to Friday's CPI (2.5% energy, 4.2% motor fuel) mean the shock lands as a hard inflation number, therefore equity options (GS's ~1% Friday straddle) are pricing almost none of it, and a 'long $USO and $XLE call ... published last week, against a futures market priced for the strait reopening, has settled at triple-digit crude' is cited as proof the thesis already played out. Invalidation: Friday's core print against JPM's 0.30% threshold.
why: The pulse correctly borrows DB's real 'the curve is pricing a Hormuz reopening that keeps not arriving' mechanism, but then manufactures a specific validating trade call -- a 'long $USO and $XLE call ... published last week' that 'has settled at triple-digit crude' -- that does not appear in any source document across the two days' full corpus (raw text or structured per-PDF trade-idea extractions), asserting a proof-of-thesis event no note actually provides.
